why: This is not a component, it is a ~/.claude/bin toolbox: 13 unrelated Python executables with no shared library, no package, no __init__, no tests in the directory, and no single job to defend. Judged file by file, off-the-shelf tools genuinely win for roughly a third of the lines and I am saying so: pii-scrub.py is a 13-regex scanner that gitleaks (with --redact, which covers its one real safety property of never printing the matched value) and Microsoft Presidio both beat on detection quality, and its national-id-shaped pattern `(?<!\d)\d{9}(?!\d)` (pii-scrub.py:96-100) fires on any nine-digit number while its tabular-pii-header pattern fires on the literal word `email` in any file, so it is a false-positive machine that a maintained scanner replaces outright; a2a-gemini-call.py plus a2a-audit.py are a hand-rolled Gemini POST and a hand-rolled JSONL call log, which is exactly simonw/llm (Apache-2.0, logs prompts and responses to SQLite by default, confirmed from its README) minus the maintenance; generate-voice.py hand-builds the ElevenLabs REST body that the official elevenlabs-python SDK and elevenlabs-mcp already wrap with retry and rate-limit handling; hive-review-dashboard.py is a SQL-to-markdown renderer over a SQLite file that Datasette serves with zero code; and backfill-allowed-tools.py (42 lines) is a one-shot migration whose 15-entry skill map has already been applied and should simply be deleted. What survives is a much smaller set, and the property holding it up is narrow and specific: external-review-judge.py (948 lines, 29% of the directory) is the only thing here that gates whether code is permitted to leave the machine at all, on a signed local attestation with an expiry. It refuses to send a bundle to Gemini unless ~/.gemini/free-tier-attestation.json says billing_tier=free AND billing_linked=false AND key_sha256 matches the exact key in this process AND the attestation is under 30 days old (external-review-judge.py:662-690), it applies a strictly wider egress blocklist to the free-tier provider than to the paid one so that resume, recruiting, candidate, customer and production-data paths are refused for Gemini but not for Codex (external-review-judge.py:60-64, 308-311, 405-408), and it hashes the full repository state before and after the review and discards every verdict from every provider if the tree moved underneath it (external-review-judge.py:449-465, 876-880), which is the same anti-staleness property tools/gate's tree_fingerprint has and which no reviewer found in the searches documents. CodeRabbit CLI, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI all review a local diff and all emit structured JSON; none of them documents a billing-tier attestation, a per-provider egress policy, or a mid-review tree-change abort, and CodeRabbit's model is that your code does reach their servers. So: adopt for the scanner, the model bridges, the TTS and the dashboard; keep external-review-judge.py and the four small files that are bound to Claude Code hook payload shapes; and treat jira-reminder-refresh.py as the unresolved one, argued in the counterargument below.

alternatives.name: Codex CLI (OpenAI, github.com/openai/codex) — `codex exec --output-schema`, plus its own `/review`
alternatives.covers: Almost the entire review mechanism external-review-judge.py wraps. The wrapper does not implement review at all — it shells out to this binary (external-review-judge.py:473-483, 603-626), so Codex already supplies the model call, the read-only sandbox, the ephemeral session, and schema-constrained JSON output. A 2026 practitioner writeup (codex.danielvaughan.com, 2026-03-27) describes local `/review` before commit plus JSON-schema output feeding quality gates, i.e. the same shape.
alternatives.gap: It reviews what you point it at; it has no opinion about whether that content is allowed to leave the machine. Concretely missing and checkable: (a) no billing-tier attestation file with an expiry gating the call — external-review-judge.py:662-690 refuses to send anything if the local attestation is over ATTESTATION_MAX_AGE_DAYS=30 or its key_sha256 does not match the key in the current process; (b) no per-provider path blocklist — external-review-judge.py:60-64 blocks resume/cv/candidate/recruiting/customer/production-data paths for one provider and not the other; (c) no before/after repository-state hash that voids the verdict if the tree changed mid-review (external-review-judge.py:876-880); (d) no rejection of a self-inconsistent judge response — parse_review_json raises if the model returns verdict=pass together with findings (external-review-judge.py:583-584). I did not verify Codex CLI's current flag surface against its own docs this session; I read only the flags this wrapper passes.
alternatives.cost: Already installed and already a hard dependency — the wrapper exits if it is absent (external-review-judge.py:480-482). Adopting more of it removes Python, adds no new install. Requires ChatGPT subscription auth; the wrapper deliberately strips OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY and four more from the child environment (external-review-judge.py:486-500) so an API-key fallback cannot silently bill.
alternatives.maturity: Actively developed per 2026 third-party writeups found in search. I did not check its release feed, changelog, or whether the flags used here are still current — that is the single most likely way this file breaks.

alternatives.name: CodeRabbit CLI (coderabbit.ai/cli, docs.coderabbit.ai/cli)
alternatives.covers: Reviews staged, unstaged and uncommitted local edits and emits structured JSON in agent mode for exactly this kind of integration. Free tier exists. This is the closest product-shaped competitor to external-review-judge.py's job.
alternatives.gap: Its own FAQ frames privacy as encryption, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and an opt-out of data storage — i.e. your code does go to their servers and the control is a vendor promise, not a local refusal. This repo's requirement is the inverse: a local file that must be under 30 days old and fingerprint-bound before a single byte is transmitted, and a path blocklist that hard-fails on resume/candidate/customer paths (external-review-judge.py:405-408). It also has no mid-review tree-change abort, and its free tier is rate-limited to 3 reviews/hour per its own blog, which a Stop-hook-driven loop would hit. I did not verify whether it can run fully offline or against a local model.
alternatives.cost: Free tier with an account; requires network and a vendor account. Adds a third-party service to a path that currently only touches a locally-installed binary and one Google API endpoint.
alternatives.maturity: Commercial, actively marketed, 2026 pricing and docs pages live. I verified the existence and free-tier claim from its own pages via search summaries only; I did not install it or test a review.

alternatives.name: Gitleaks (github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) — with detect-secrets and TruffleHog as the adjacent pair
alternatives.covers: Replaces pii-scrub.py's secrets half entirely, and would also be a better implementation of external-review-judge.py's SECRET_PATTERNS pre-send check (external-review-judge.py:39-51, 314-317). Critically it covers pii-scrub.py's one genuine safety property: `--redact` (and `--redact=N` for partial) hides the matched value in output, which is the exact reason pii-scrub.py:189-191 prints only `file:line <pattern-name>`. TruffleHog additionally verifies whether a found credential is still live, which neither this repo nor gitleaks does.
alternatives.gap: It scans for secrets, not PII. It would not replace pii-scrub.py's email / Israeli-phone / national-ID / tabular-header patterns (pii-scrub.py:76-107) — those need Presidio or equivalent, so adopting gitleaks alone means running two tools. It also has no in-place `--redact`-the-file mode equivalent to pii-scrub.py:173-181, which rewrites the file with `<REDACTED>`; gitleaks redacts its own report, not your document. Adding a Go binary breaks the stdlib-only, zero-install habit the rest of this repo keeps.
alternatives.cost: Single static Go binary, MIT, Windows-friendly, no runtime deps. Real but small install weight. Pairs naturally with pre-commit.
alternatives.maturity: Two 2026 comparison writeups found (rafter.so, appsecsanta.com) treat gitleaks and TruffleHog as the two dominant OSS scanners with ~51k combined stars. I did not verify that star figure, any benchmark number, or the current release version myself.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Presidio (github.com/microsoft/presidio, presidio-analyzer + presidio-anonymizer)
alternatives.covers: The PII half of pii-scrub.py, properly: NER via spaCy or HuggingFace transformers plus pattern matching plus contextual scoring, with a real anonymizer engine, custom recognizers, and per-country packs. It would eliminate the false-positive behaviour of pii-scrub.py's bare nine-digit and bare-keyword patterns.
alternatives.gap: Heavy for a Stop-hook-latency path: it wants a spaCy or transformers model loaded, which is a multi-hundred-MB download and seconds of import time, against a script whose whole job is to exit non-zero fast. It also has no Israeli-phone or Israeli-ID recognizer in the predefined set as far as I could tell — a search summary listed a Philippines PH_TIN recognizer and a German DE_* pack as recent additions, with no IL pack mentioned — so the two locale-specific patterns at pii-scrub.py:83-94 would still be hand-written custom recognizers. I did not verify the predefined-recognizer list against the repo.
alternatives.cost: pip install plus an NLP model; MIT licence. Materially heavier than 201 lines of `re`. Reasonable as a batch/CI gate, questionable inside a hook.
alternatives.maturity: A 2026 guide and the PyPI page report an active June 2026 release with named June 2026 changes. I did not open the releases page to confirm that date independently — I am relying on a search summary.

alternatives.name: simonw/llm (github.com/simonw/llm, Apache-2.0) with llm-gemini and llm-openai-plugin
alternatives.covers: a2a-gemini-call.py (40 lines) and a2a-audit.py (132 lines) in one dependency. Verified from the repo README this session: it stores prompts and responses in SQLite by default, which is a strictly better substrate than the append-only JSONL at a2a-audit.py:36-57 and the hand-rolled aggregation loop at a2a-audit.py:73-101. Plugin architecture covers OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Llama, Ollama and local models.
alternatives.gap: It has no path to the Azure AI Foundry endpoints a2a-foundry-call.py actually calls — the Applications endpoint `/applications/<agent>/responses` and the `{"agent": {"name": ..., "type": "agent_reference"}}` envelope (a2a-foundry-call.py:53, 83-88, 119-124) — and no `az account get-access-token --resource https://cognitiveservices.azure.com` bearer flow (a2a-foundry-call.py:58-75). I searched specifically for llm plus Azure plus SQLite audit and found only third-party gateways (LiteLLM, Bifrost) for Azure routing, not first-party support. So adopting llm retires the Gemini bridge and the audit log but leaves the 216-line Foundry bridge, which is the one with a genuinely non-standard endpoint shape.
alternatives.cost: pip install, Apache-2.0, plus a plugin per provider. Replaces two files with a dependency plus config. Its SQLite log lives in its own location, so anything reading ~/.claude/cache/a2a/audit.jsonl today (self-improve.py:99-104 counts its lines) has to be repointed.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained, 1110 commits on main per the README fetched this session. I did not check the latest release version or date, and I did not verify that llm-gemini currently supports the responseJsonSchema structured-output field external-review-judge.py:721-729 depends on.

alternatives.name: Claude Code statusline ecosystem — ccstatusline (sirmalloc/ccstatusline, npm), CCometixLine (Rust), cc-statusline, ccusage statusline
alternatives.covers: The rendering job of subagent-hud.py (70 lines) and, outside this component's Python, statusline.sh. These are mature, themeable, powerline-capable, and already parse the Claude Code statusline payload; ccusage adds real quota, burn-rate and cost tracking that this repo does not have at all.
alternatives.gap: subagent-hud.py renders `subagentStatusLine` — the per-agent panel rows, reading `tasks[]` with id/status/model/tokenCount/label from stdin and emitting one `{"id":..., "content":...}` JSON line per row (subagent-hud.py:49-66). That is a different hook contract from the main `statusLine`. I did NOT verify that any of these tools implements subagentStatusLine; every description I found is about the main status line. That is the exact checkable question a future session should settle — if ccstatusline supports subagentStatusLine, delete subagent-hud.py. It also pairs each status colour with a word rather than colour alone (subagent-hud.py:27-38), a deliberate colourblind-safety rule I did not verify these tools follow.
alternatives.cost: npx / npm or a Rust binary; adds a Node or Rust dependency to a path that is currently 70 lines of stdlib Python that fails silent on bad input. Non-trivial for a statusline that must never hang the terminal.
alternatives.maturity: Several actively maintained competitors listed in hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code and compared in a 2026 writeup (yigitkonur.com). I did not install any of them or verify their release cadence.

alternatives.name: n8n (n8n.io) — with Jira's own native automation rules as the lighter option
alternatives.covers: Essentially all of jira-reminder-refresh.py (909 lines, 28% of this directory): scheduled trigger, Jira JQL query, Azure Monitor / Application Insights nodes, branching logic, HTML digest, email send. n8n publishes ready-made templates for exactly this — 'Generate daily Jira summaries & weekly reports with Azure OpenAI and Gmail' and a Jira-Software-plus-Azure-Monitor integration page. A 2026 comparison piece states the rule directly: use Jira's built-in rules when the logic stays inside Jira, use n8n when it crosses tools, which this does.
alternatives.gap: n8n stores credentials in its own credential store on a running instance; this script pulls the Jira token and the Brevo SMTP login from Azure Key Vault at call time and never writes them to disk (jira-reminder-refresh.py:74-85, docstring lines 9-11), and raises a local flag file when the az session needs interactive re-login so the SessionStart banner can surface it (jira-reminder-refresh.py:88-98). It also writes a local JSON digest that a Claude Code SessionStart hook reads cheaply — an n8n workflow would have to write that file back to this machine, which means either self-hosting n8n locally or opening an inbound path. And the ~190-line HTML report renderer (jira-reminder-refresh.py:577-767) with its risk scoring (516-576) is bespoke content, not plumbing; n8n replaces the wiring, not the report.
alternatives.cost: Self-hosted n8n is a Node service plus a database plus a persistent process, or a paid cloud tier. That is a large standing dependency for one cron job on one laptop. Jira native automation rules are free and zero-install but cannot reach Azure Monitor at all.
alternatives.maturity: Widely used, large public template library, 2026 integration pages live. I did not verify licensing terms (n8n uses a source-available Sustainable Use Licence, which I did not read this session) or whether the Azure Monitor node exposes the App Insights analytics-query call this script relies on (jira-reminder-refresh.py:124-146).

alternatives.name: Datasette (datasette.io, by the simonw/llm author)
alternatives.covers: hive-review-dashboard.py (157 lines) in full and then some. That file opens ~/.hive/beads.db, runs four fixed SELECTs (hive-review-dashboard.py:54-81) and formats them as markdown tables. Datasette serves any SQLite file as a browsable, queryable, JSON-API-backed web UI with no code, and canned queries would cover the four fixed ones.
alternatives.gap: Datasette serves a web UI; this script writes a static markdown file to ~/.claude/docs/HIVE_REVIEW_PICKUP_STATUS.md (hive-review-dashboard.py:12, 151) that an agent can read from disk with no server running — which is the actual consumption pattern here. It also would not do the second half: shelling out to `git log --since` across six named project repos and appending those commits to the same document (hive-review-dashboard.py:32-48, 142-149). That is a join across SQLite and six git repos, which is not a Datasette job.
alternatives.cost: pip install plus a running process, or `datasette --get` for one-shot rendering. Apache-2.0.
alternatives.maturity: Long-established and actively maintained. I did not verify its current release or test it against this schema; I did not open ~/.hive/beads.db.

alternatives.name: ElevenLabs official Python SDK (github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python) and elevenlabs-mcp (github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-mcp)
alternatives.covers: generate-voice.py (159 lines). The script hand-builds the /v1/text-to-speech POST body with voice_settings and language_code (generate-voice.py:~105-140) against a hard-coded table of eight voice IDs and stability/similarity presets (generate-voice.py:36-46). The official SDK wraps the same REST endpoints and, per the MCP repo description, handles rate limiting, retry logic and error reporting — none of which this script does.
alternatives.gap: Two behaviours would have to be reimplemented on top: the Hebrew/Arabic Unicode-range sniff that auto-switches model from eleven_multilingual_v2 to eleven_v3 and sets language_code, because multilingual_v2 mispronounces Hebrew as Arabic (generate-voice.py:31-32 and the auto-detect block) — that is a real defect this operator hit, and it is a policy the SDK has no reason to hold; and fetching the API key from Azure Key Vault `kv-seekapa-apps` rather than an env var (generate-voice.py:49-59). The MCP server is also the wrong shape for a shell-callable script that prints a markdown link and auto-plays.
alternatives.cost: pip install; MIT for the SDK. Replaces ~100 lines of urllib with a dependency. The MCP server additionally needs an MCP client and a running process.
alternatives.maturity: Official, first-party. A search summary reports the MCP server launched 2026-07-06 and its repo was last updated 2026-07-23; I did not confirm either date against the repository myself, and I did not check the SDK's version or Python support matrix.

evidence: Read in full this session: external-review-judge.py:1-949 (in three passes: 1-260, 260-660, 660-949), a2a-audit.py:1-133, pii-scrub.py:1-202, self-improve.py:1-132, a2a-foundry-call.py:1-217, hive-review-dashboard.py:1-158, gastown-spawn.py:1-150, jira-time-stop.py:1-149, subagent-hud.py:1-71, backfill-allowed-tools.py:1-43, a2a-gemini-call.py:1-41. Read partially: generate-voice.py:1-110 of 159 (docstring, voice table, key fetch, arg parsing, language auto-detect, request body) — I did not read the response-handling and auto-play tail. Read partially and deliberately: jira-reminder-refresh.py:1-140 line by line, plus a complete grep index of all 27 function definitions spanning lines 70-877 — I did NOT read lines 140-909 line by line, in particular the ~190-line HTML renderer at 577-767 and the SMTP send at 860-876, so my description of those is from their names, signatures and surrounding constants, not from reading their bodies. LOC verified by `wc -l`: 3302 Python across 13 files, plus 2038 lines of shell and 250 lines of extensionless scripts in the same directory that are OUT of this record's scope. Also read docs/prior-art/tools-gate.json:1-72 as the format exemplar. Searches run (9 WebSearch + 1 WebFetch): 'local CLI AI code review uncommitted diff Codex Gemini judge structured JSON output self-hosted'; 'Claude Code hooks statusline plugin marketplace community scripts ccstatusline ccusage'; 'gitleaks TruffleHog detect-secrets Microsoft Presidio PII redaction CLI compare 2026'; 'simonw llm CLI multi-provider plugin Gemini Azure OpenAI logs sqlite audit'; 'Jira automation rules vs n8n cron digest email Azure Application Insights daily report script'; 'LLM-as-a-judge code review prompt injection untrusted diff sandbox research paper 2026'; 'awesome-claude-code repository hooks statusline scripts collection list'; 'CodeRabbit CLI free tier does it send code to servers privacy local review'; 'Microsoft Presidio anonymizer maintained 2026 release PII detection Python library'; 'ElevenLabs official Python SDK MCP server text-to-speech CLI 2026'; 'gitleaks --redact flag hide secret value output pre-commit protect staged'; plus WebFetch of github.com/simonw/llm confirming Apache-2.0 and SQLite-logging-by-default. NOT VERIFIED, plainly: I installed and ran nothing — no gitleaks, no Presidio, no llm, no ccstatusline, no CodeRabbit, no Datasette, no n8n. I did not execute a single one of the 13 scripts, so I have no evidence any of them currently runs on this machine; several import from ~/projects/intent-control-plane/src (self-improve.py:27-29, jira-time-stop.py:68-69) and one hard-codes a Linux path /home/shovalbe/.claude/bin/intent (gastown-spawn.py:25) that cannot resolve on this Windows host, which I noticed but did not test. There are no tests anywhere in this directory. No star count, benchmark number, pricing figure or release date in this record was verified beyond the search summary that produced it. The academic search on LLM-as-a-judge prompt injection returned real arXiv work (2505.13348, 2504.18333 and others) confirming the threat external-review-judge.py's SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION defends against at lines 125-140, but I did not read any of those papers and make no claim about whether that defence is effective.
recheck: Run all four; any one flipping re-opens the verdict. (1) Is the keep-half still unique? `WebSearch "codex OR coderabbit OR gemini-cli review egress policy attestation billing tier free data retention refuse"` and `WebSearch "AI code review CLI abort verdict repository changed during review state hash"` — if any shipping reviewer documents a local attestation-with-expiry gating transmission, or a mid-review tree-change abort, external-review-judge.py:662-690 and :876-880 lose their justification. (2) Is the HUD still bespoke? `WebSearch "ccstatusline subagentStatusLine"` and `WebFetch https://github.com/sirmalloc/ccstatusline` asking whether it implements subagentStatusLine — if yes, delete subagent-hud.py. (3) Has the adopt-half been acted on? `wc -l ~/claude-setup/dot-claude/bin/*.py` — if pii-scrub.py, a2a-gemini-call.py, a2a-audit.py, generate-voice.py, hive-review-dashboard.py and backfill-allowed-tools.py (705 lines together) are still present and unchanged, this record was filed and ignored, which is the failure mode it exists to prevent. (4) Are the alternatives still alive? `gh release list --repo gitleaks/gitleaks --limit 3; gh release list --repo microsoft/presidio --limit 3; gh release list --repo simonw/llm --limit 3; gh release list --repo elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python --limit 3` — read-only gh, no quota spend.
what_ours_does: Thirteen independent executables, no shared module, no tests. (1) external-review-judge.py (948 lines, 29%) runs Codex and/or Gemini as fail-closed independent code-review judges: run_bounded (external-review-judge.py:170-242) executes children with file-backed stdout/stderr capture, polls their size against a hard cap, and kills the whole process tree on Windows via `taskkill /PID n /T /F` (147-168); build_bundle (332-465) assembles a size-capped git diff plus untracked text files, refuses binaries, symlinks and oversized files (320-329), blocks credential-shaped paths for both providers and additionally resume/cv/candidate/recruiting/customer/production-data paths for Gemini (60-64, 308-311, 405-408), scans the assembled bundle for nine credential shapes before transmission (39-51, 314-317), and returns a sha256 over head/base/status/diff/criteria/untracked-contents; command_review (842-902) recomputes that hash after the judges return and, on any change, throws away every verdict (876-880); parse_review_json (521-585) hand-validates the response against an exact key set and rejects verdict=pass alongside non-empty findings (583-584); read_attestation (662-690) is the egress gate described above; codex_environment (486-500) strips eight API-key and endpoint variables so Codex must use ChatGPT subscription auth (588-591); safe_output_path (782-792) confines all writes under <repo>/.claude/reviews; aggregate (764-779) emits a distinct 'disagreement' state and a hard-coded auto_apply=false. (2) jira-reminder-refresh.py (909 lines, 28%) is a cron job: Key-Vault-at-runtime secret fetch with an AzAuthError that distinguishes 'needs interactive az login' from a transient failure (74-85) and drops a flag file the SessionStart banner surfaces (88-98); a JQL pull of open assigned tickets (67, 100-107); four Application Insights components queried for usage, storage, platform metrics and container-job status (44-49, 124-146, 182-365); an Azure activity digest filtered to write/delete/role-assignment/key operations (51-54, 366-399); risk scoring (516-576); a ~190-line HTML report (577-767); and a Brevo SMTP send (860-876). It writes nothing back to Jira. (3) a2a-foundry-call.py (216) bridges to Azure AI Foundry agents over two different endpoint envelopes — the Applications path and the raw Responses API with an agent_reference (78-145) — authenticating with an az-issued bearer token (58-75) and logging every call. (4) pii-scrub.py (201) is a 13-pattern check/redact gate that prints location and pattern name only, never the matched value (32-107, 189-191). (5) generate-voice.py (159) is ElevenLabs TTS with an eight-voice preset table and a Hebrew/Arabic Unicode sniff that switches model to eleven_v3 because multilingual_v2 mispronounces Hebrew as Arabic. (6) hive-review-dashboard.py (157) joins four SELECTs over ~/.hive/beads.db with `git log --since` across six named repos into one markdown status file (23-29, 32-48, 51-153). (7) gastown-spawn.py (149) spawns a persona through claude_agent_sdk and streams one line per tool call to stderr and a per-agent log so agents are never headless (51-88), optionally runs a draft/self-critique/revise loop (122-135), and grades the resulting git diff through a tested package, catching every exception so grading can never break a spawn (94-111). (8) jira-time-stop.py (148) is a Stop hook computing active-engagement time as the sum of inter-event transcript gaps each capped at 300s so AFK time cannot inflate it (44-61), attributing it to the current ticket only if a separate assessor agrees the work was related (64-108), appending to a pending ledger that is never posted without human confirmation, and returning 0 on any failure so it can never break the Stop chain (111-115). (9) a2a-audit.py (132) is the append-only JSONL call log plus tail/stats. (10) self-improve.py (131) writes a dated advisory report — never mutating config — scoring intents against evidence, listing skills unreachable from the router, and asking Codex for one reflective proposal; it imports its pure logic from a tested package rather than duplicating untested glue (24-29) and reports eval-gate results per repo because the global log conflates repos (64-79). (11) subagent-hud.py (70) renders agent-panel rows, always pairing a status colour with a status word (27-38). (12) a2a-gemini-call.py (40) is a bare Gemini POST framed as the decorrelated second reviewer. (13) backfill-allowed-tools.py (42) is a spent one-shot migration that rewrote allowed-tools frontmatter on 15 named skills.
strongest_counterargument: The verdict is doing something slightly dishonest with scope. Asked to audit 3302 lines, I have defended 948 of them on three real properties, conceded ~705 to off-the-shelf tools, and parked the second-largest file — jira-reminder-refresh.py, 909 lines, 28% of the directory — in a 'keep' bucket it has not earned. Read the gap I wrote for n8n again: everything I claimed n8n cannot do is a consequence of choosing to run this on one laptop as a cron job. Key Vault at runtime is not a property n8n lacks, it is a property n8n would express as a credential node against the same vault. The local flag file and the local digest JSON are only necessary because a local SessionStart banner reads them, and if the digest were emailed or posted, the banner is a nice-to-have, not a requirement. The 190-line HTML renderer is not evidence of an irreplaceable property, it is evidence that someone spent an afternoon on an email template — replaceable by any templating step in any workflow tool, and honestly by a plain-text digest. Strip that file out and the directory is ~2400 lines, of which ~705 are conceded and 948 rest on properties that themselves depend on Codex CLI staying flag-compatible; the residual genuinely-bespoke Python is closer to 700 lines than to 3302. Second, and worse: I marked nothing 'dead' except a 42-line migration script, but I also could not execute a single file, and gastown-spawn.py:25 hard-codes /home/shovalbe/.claude/bin/intent, a Linux path that cannot exist on this Windows host. A file that cannot run is not a component to keep or adopt away, it is rot, and the correct action is deletion or a documented WSL-only marker — not a prior-art record that quietly counts its 149 lines toward the total being defended. A future session should assume the true adopt surface here is larger than this record admits, and should start by running every one of these thirteen scripts with --help and deleting the ones that fail.
_scope: Scoped to the 13 .py files in dot-claude/bin (3302 lines, verified by wc -l). The 21 shell scripts (2038 lines, including statusline.sh at 340 and deploy-setup.sh at 253) and the 5 extensionless launchers (250 lines) in the same directory are NOT covered and need their own record.
